tickets.title: Lifted `match` in a partial function and in the REPL gives E-MATCH-MOTIVE: resolve its draft there

Repro (release binary, 21 Oct):
  def f (n: Nat): {Partial} Nat :=
    let r := match n with | 0 => 1 | Succ m => m
    if r == 3 then 0 else f (n + 1)
and, in `stitchwort repl`, `(match 2 with | 0 => 1 | Succ m => m) + 1`.

Scope: resolve drafts for (a) and (c), the two a user can hit. (b) may stay refused, with a message that says why (a data or ability declaration has nowhere to put the helper). tickets.title: Lambda postponing in effectful calls
tickets.where: Fixed by 6dc28126 (SW-223); cases added in examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw
tickets.body:
Problem: a lambda argument whose parameter type is fixed by a later argument is postponed in pure calls (check.rs:903-970, examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw), but not in effectful ones. Repro (type Person = { name: Text, age: Nat }):

    def appIO (f: a -> {IO} b) (x: a): {IO} b := f x
    def e1 (p: Person): {IO} Text := appIO (q => q.name) p
    -- E-CANNOT-INFER: can't tell what `q` is, so can't look up `.name`

The same call written with `appP` (no `{IO}` in the callback type) checks. A pure call placed after an effectful statement in the same block (`IO.print "x"` then `appP (q => q.name) p`) also fails. Cause (not yet confirmed): effectful calls apply arguments one at a time (crates/elab/src/effects.rs comp_call) and never go through apply_args_postponing.

First step: confirm the cause in effects.rs, then reuse the postponing path for calls whose arguments perform operations.

Done when: the repro above and a pure-after-effect variant check, with a test in examples/accept/ (extend lambda-postponed.sw) and the gate green.

tickets.title: More tail calls as loops in generated JS
tickets.body:
Only a function's calls to itself (including in either branch of a plain `if`) become loops today (self_tail_loop, crates/js/src/lib.rs:1430). A tail call inside `if h: P then a else b` is not recognised, because it is generated as `Decidable.elim … (v => a) (v => b)`; the same goes for helpers like `maybeThen`.

Repro (release binary, 21 Oct): scratch file
  def loopH (acc: Nat): Nat -> Nat
    | 0      => acc
    | Succ n => if h: n = 7 then acc else loopH (acc + 1) n
  export def count (n: Nat): Nat := loopH 0 n
built with `stitchwort build --js`; `count(1000000n)` throws `StitchwortResourceError: count: ran out of resources (Maximum call stack size exceeded)`. (The `if h:` here is a Decidable elimination, so the case tree does not see a tail position.)

First step: decide whether to treat `Decidable.elim` applications with lambda branches as an `if` in the tail analysis (crates/js/src/lib.rs:1617 `tail`) or to generate `if h:` as a conditional in the first place. Calls between different functions are SW-49.

Done when: the repro above, with 10^7 in place of 10^6, runs; an examples/extract file covers `if h:` in tail position.

tickets.title: WebAssembly stack guard: measure limits in all browsers (incl. compact text) and choose the guard size
tickets.body:
Problem: each call uses stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8); the engine's runs out first, so the guard is 128 KiB (crates/web/build.rs:19, override STITCHWORT_GUARD at :33), calibrated in Node and Chrome only. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured. 128 KiB gives about 25 levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements; 256 KiB would roughly double that with a 2x margin in Node. The parser's stack use per level could also be cut (e.g. boxing `Diagnostic` in its `Result`): that is SW-126.

Change, one campaign: measure in all four engines with web/stress.html: nesting depth, long list/text literals (including compact `List Char` literals, d4d3626, which were only measured natively: the limit before E-RESOURCE and the time), then pick the guard size.

Eliminating recursion (stack-safe-evaluation steps 3 and 4, docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md) is the real fix; see also SW-62 (long literals) and SW-57 (JS limits in browsers, different subject: generated code).

Done when: a table of limits per browser (nesting, literal length, compact text) is in docs/evaluator-speed.md or compact-text.md and the guard is set from it.

WARNING, read before starting (Matt, 30 Oct 2026; from the kernel research register, docs/research/kernel.md §5.1, read in full texts): the recursive-proposition trap. If a proposition can be eliminated into data AND holds a proof of itself in a field, definitional proof irrelevance makes conversion undecidable: any proof X can be unfolded once more, X ≡ MkLoop (Loop.inv X), with no bound on how many unfoldings conversion must try (Gilbert et al. POPL19 §2.3; Abel & Coquand; Lean answered with lean4#13851/#14977). Stitchwort accepts such a type TODAY: E-PROP-ELIM (crates/core/src/check.rs:915-929) lets a single-constructor Prop whose fields are all Prop eliminate into data, without asking whether a field mentions the type itself. Checked by the orchestrator on 30 Oct with main's binary: `type Loop: Prop = | MkLoop (next: Loop)` with `def steps (l: Loop): Nat := match l with | MkLoop n => Succ (steps n)` checks. It is harmless now (no definitional irrelevance yet), but becomes the trap once D1′ masks proof positions. proof-irrelevance.md §5.1 currently defends Loop by making D1′ deliberately incomplete; the register recommends closing the hole instead: add a condition to E-PROP-ELIM that no constructor field mentions the type itself (Lean's rule), after measuring that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue relies on it (register ticket T2; decision D1980, open). Do this BEFORE or AS PART OF stage 1, with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.


D1980 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): yes, refuse eliminating a self-referential proposition into data (the warning above), but as part of THIS ticket's work, not before it: when SW-93 starts, measure first that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue eliminates such a proposition into data, then add the E-PROP-ELIM condition with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.
Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct): record eta interacts with this ticket. Once proofs are irrelevant, a record whose fields are all proofs behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. POPL26, Rocq requires a relevant field). If record eta (SW-55/SW-789) exists or lands after this, it must be limited to records with at least one field that isn't a proof.

tickets.title: Effect-polymorphic calls don't pass the expected type to their arguments (orElse 0 at Int)

Workaround: `orElse (0: Int)`. Found by SW-217 (examples/accept/abort.sw notes it).

Roguelike per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: step calls next() once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) …, Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling roll freely. Why: then seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants (walls, HP, occupancy, stepValid, replayValid) are proved about pure resolve for every seed. Free roll would lose them until proofs through a handler stop stepping symbolically into E-RESOURCE (see the handler-stepping ticket; Effect.bindAssoc axiom). Found by the SW-685 elaborator fuzzer (oracle 2, no E-INTERNAL). Seeds/cases: default 0x5eede1ab00000685 case 5981 (accept/quot-forms.sw); 0x2 case 3085 (accept/index-proof-conflict-data.sw); 0xabcdef cases 568 and 1084. All the same shape after reduction: a type's constructor (or an index type) names a later declaration that in turn names the type, so the declarations form a cycle the order check doesn't catch. Minimal input:

def Q: Type := List T
type T: Q → Type =
  | A: T Nil

gives '[E-INTERNAL] internal error: `Q` is used before it's checked', 'this is a bug in the compiler'. Variants: 'type Vec (a: Type): Nat → Type = | VCons (x: a) (xs: Vec a n): Box a (Succ n)' followed by 'type Box: Type 1 = | Mk [a: Type] (xs: List a) (rest: Vec)' (E-INTERNAL on Box); a theorem 'noAB: SameP A B → Void' used by an earlier type's constructor and mentioning that type (E-INTERNAL on noAB). Expected: an ordinary cyclic-dependency error (the code for mutually recursive declarations that aren't declared together) at the use.

tickets.title: Kernel's E-TYPE-MISMATCH reaches the user for a Comp whose result row is an unbound variable (elaborator lets an ill-typed term through)
tickets.body:
Found by the SW-685 elaborator fuzzer (oracle 3, the kernel never rejects an elaborated term; seed 0x1 case 1633, from reject/empty-row-function.sw). Minimal input:

import Std.Effect (Comp, NoOp)
def next (n: Nat): Comp NoOp r Nat := n + 1

The error ('[E-TYPE-MISMATCH] type mismatch ... expected Comp Effect.NoOp r Nat, but this has type Comp Effect.NoOp Effect.NoRes Nat') is the kernel's, not the elaborator's: stitchwort_elab::take_kernel_rejections (the hook SW-685 adds in crates/elab/src/kernel.rs) records the same message from a define call. So the elaborator accepted `n + 1` against a type with an auto-bound variable `r` (it should have reported the mismatch itself, or failed to unify NoRes with the rigid `r`). Severity is low: the user still gets a reasonable error, only from the wrong layer. The fuzzer oracle flags any kernel E-MALFORMED/E-TYPE-MISMATCH/E-NOT-A-* whose message reaches the user unchanged.

Deliberate literature trawl for ideas to steal: dependently typed language implementation and effect systems. Started 29 Oct at Matt's request (first: effects, elaboration).

D1830 (Matt, 29 Oct): yes, all seven clusters, two or three lanes at a time, starting with effects and elaboration.
D1831 (Matt, 29 Oct): 2022 cutoff for now (venue sweep 2022-2026, snowballing within that); may go deeper later.

Clusters (with board hooks):
1. Kernel/type theory: rewrite rules, definitional proof irrelevance (SProp), record eta, observational TT, quotients, universe polymorphism (SW-787, SW-55/789, SW-93/803).
2. Inductive types and recursion: nested, inductive-inductive, QIITs; size-change termination, well-founded recursion, guard checking (SW-704, SW-199).
3. Elaboration: unification (pattern fragment, postponement), implicits, glued evaluation, Kovacs elaboration-zoo/smalltt, error messages (SW-509, 553, 817, 859).
4. Proof automation: simp-style rewriting, decision procedures, reflection, e-graphs, omega/ring, counterexample search (rewrite/cases friction in AoC notes).
5. Effects and handlers: row typing, evidence passing (Koka), capability passing (Effekt), lexical handlers, OCaml 5, handler termination, effects + dependent types (Ahman, F*, ExTT) (SW-790-792, effect-runtime notes, handler-termination conjecture).
6. Compilation and runtime: erasure, Perceus/FBIP, Lean IR, interpreter design, WASM/JS (SW-813, native backend).
7. Infrastructure and trust: content-addressed code (Unison), query-based incremental compilers, kernel fuzzing/testing, mechanised kernels (MetaRocq, Lean4Lean) (check cache, SW-684-689).

Sources: POPL, PLDI, ICFP, OOPSLA, ESOP, ECOOP, CPP, ITP, TYPES, FSCD, TyDe, HOPE, ML workshop, CoqPL/RocqPL, Lean workshops; arXiv cs.PL/cs.LO; Lean/Agda/Rocq/Idris2/Koka/Effekt/Flix/OCaml/Unison/Roc release notes and RFCs; snowballing from LFST, Taming of the Rew, Allais-McBride-Boutillier, Koka evidence passing, Perceus; blogs (Kovacs, Cockx, Danielsson, Leijen, Brachthauser).

Pipeline: harvest per cluster (record queries) -> screen on title/abstract against hooks (keep/maybe/drop) -> ~5-line card per kept paper (claim, what to steal, which ticket/note, cost: small/kernel/research, links, full text reachable?) -> deep-read top 3-5 per cluster -> ticket or design note, never straight to code.
Output: docs/research/ (one file per cluster + ranked "steal next" index); new tickets labelled research for ideas that pass; short summary to Matt with at most a couple of decisions. Lanes screen ~40-80 papers, deep-read up to 5. Quarterly light refresh from saved queries.

29 Oct: REDO ALL SEVEN CLUSTERS with full-text reading (Matt). First four registers (effects, elaboration, proof automation, kernel) relied partly on abstracts: no PDF tool was used. tickets.title: Literature research: lessons (how NOT to run it) and where the partial results are; PAUSED
tickets.body:
PAUSED (Matt, 29 Oct 2026). Literature trawl SW-894 went badly. This ticket records how NOT to run it, and where the partial results are. Restart only on Matt's say-so, ONE lane at a time.

== What went wrong (don't repeat) ==
1. Lanes couldn't read papers and nobody checked first. No PDF tool is installed (pdftotext, mutool, qpdf absent) and WebFetch can't read PDFs. Elaboration, proof automation and kernel registers were written largely from abstracts. Fix that works (tested): `nix shell nixpkgs#poppler-utils -c pdftotext paper.pdf -` (package name has a hyphen; `poppler_utils` is the old name and fails). Test the toolchain on a real paper BEFORE starting a lane.
2. Caveats were buried. Each lane listed "sources not reached / abstract only" at the END of its report; the orchestrator relayed the findings and rankings and dropped the caveat. Rule: every register and every report must START with counts: screened / carded / read in full / not read. Every card says "Full text: read (source)" or "NOT READ"; NOT READ supports no ranking or recommendation.
3. Unverified claims were relayed as fact. Lanes said "the session's web-search budget ran out"; the orchestrator first repeated it, then (after one successful search) wrongly said there was no budget, without checking the docs. The docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, "Session search limit"): an interactive session has 200 WebSearch calls shared with ALL subagents; at the limit searches silently do nothing; refills ~100/hour (v2.1.290+, CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR); cap raisable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION; /clear resets. Seven parallel research lanes at ~30-40 searches each exhaust it. Plan the search budget; run at most one searching lane; lanes report immediately if searches start doing nothing.
4. Too many lanes at once (up to 4, plus helpers). Stopping a lane does NOT stop the reading helpers it spawned; they kept running and reporting after "stop". After stopping a lane, check ListAgents and stop its children.
5. Decision spam: each lane asked 2-3 decisions; the orchestrator listed them all. Keep to one or two decisions at a time.
6. Personal data: the orchestrator once sent Matt's email address to the Unpaywall API (one request, DOI 10.1145/3434341). Never send personal data to any service. Use Semantic Scholar's API (no email needed) for open-access lookups.
7. Leads can be wrong: the kernel redo's readers found the first kernel register misstated papers (Géran says nothing about Lean's level normaliser; the sort-polymorphism paper doesn't use "quality variables" and mechanises nothing; the definitional-inversion paper isn't about Lean with quotients; MetaCoq found one Coq kernel incompleteness, not a soundness bug). Re-derive claims from full texts, never from a previous register.
8. Access problems that remain: ACM DL returns 403 / HTML to scripts; HAL sometimes returns a bot page (check `file x.pdf`); TU Delft repository refused connections; image-only PDFs/slides can't be read (no OCR). Keep a "for Matt to fetch" table.

== Process to use next time ==
One lane at a time. Before starting: test pdftotext on a real paper, check the WebSearch budget headroom, give the lane a reserved D-number range and the reading protocol (counts first, read in full or NOT READ, for-Matt-to-fetch table, no personal data). When it reports: verify its counts and a sample of cards against the files before relaying; lead with how much was read. Log progress as you go. Merge only after reading the diff and running the merge tier.

tickets.title: Memory blow-up: List.Mem hypothesis + failing proof + Vec-nested type
tickets.body:
`check --no-cache` on this file goes past 28 GB in about 8 s (found by the SW-704 stage 3 lane). It happens on main too: the binary built from main 82729c37 was killed by dev/memguard at 3.17 GB against a 2 GB cap (checked by the orchestrator on 30 Oct). So it isn't caused by stage 3.

    import Std (List, Nat, Vec)
    type Packet: Type = | Number (value: Nat) | Packets (items: List Packet)
    theorem smaller (items: List Packet) (q: Packet) (h: List.Mem q items): q = q := nope
    type Wide: Type = | WLeaf | WNode (kids: Vec Wide 2)

The lane found that all three parts are needed: removing `Wide`, removing `h`, or giving a working proof makes it fine. Not investigated beyond that. Always run repros under dev/memguard --cap-gb 2.

Investigation (30 Oct, lane worktree-agent-a41739081c8754ea3):
- Smaller repro, no `h`, no `Wide`, no Vec: `type Rose: Type = | Leaf | Node (kids: List Rose)` with `theorem t (q: Rose): q = q := nope`. Killed by memguard at 3.05 GB after 1.0 s CPU.
- `sample` shows 712 of 737 samples in `counterexample::search_counterexample`, inside a deep recursion of `Inputs::random` (List branch) under `Inputs::random_tuple`.
- Cause: in crates/elab/src/counterexample/inputs.rs:714-716, a random `List` gets a length of up to `size`, and every element is drawn at the full `size` again. For a rose tree this grows faster than exponentially. Debug counter: the biggest tuple per size was 4063 nodes at size 12, 134260 at 15, 466313 at 16 and 2942245 at 17, while sizes go up to RANDOM_SIZE = 40. MAX_DEPTH bounds only the depth, not the width. mod.rs:540-548 builds all the random tuples before any time check.
- Why the three parts: a failing proof (any failing proof, `:= h` too, not only an unknown name) runs the search (module.rs:580). `h: List.Mem q items` puts the theorem out of scope ("nothing decides List.Any") unless List.decMem is loaded, and any use of Vec (even `def foo: Vec Nat 0 := Vec.VNil`) loads it. So `Wide` matters only because it uses Vec. Removing `h` doesn't make it go away when `items` stays. Declaration order doesn't matter.
- Not related to derive_induct.rs or size_from_member.
- Experiment (debug commit 8b5cbbea): give each list element `size / length`. The repro then finishes in 0.14 s CPU with at most 64 nodes per tuple, and d9.sw checks in 0.83 s.
Fix lane (30 Oct, worktree-agent-acfd19afe8504e35e): list and Vec elements share the size (size / length), MAX_RANDOM_VALUES = 1000 per draw, drawing stops at the random phase's time; Rose repro 3 GB-killed -> 0.15 s CPU (1b571d5c). Next: examples, snapshots, docs.

tickets.title: SOUNDNESS: universe level overflow, Type 4294967295 : Type 0 is accepted
tickets.body:
SOUNDNESS. Found 30 Oct 2026 by the kernel-bug test lane (kernel register T1, porting Lean's looseBVarRange bit-overflow shape); reproduced by the orchestrator with main's release binary.

`def wrap: Type 0 := Type 4294967295` is ACCEPTED ("checked"). So is `def wrap2: Type 4294967295 := Type 4294967294`. (`def big: Type 4294967295 := Nat` is rightly E-UNIVERSE; `Type 4294967296` is E-PARSE "universe level is too large".)

Cause: universe levels are u32 (`crates/core/src/term.rs:24`, `Sort::Type(u32)`), and the step to the next universe adds one unchecked: the kernel's `Sort::succ` (`term.rs:32`, `Sort::Type(i) => Sort::Type(i + 1)`, used at `crates/core/src/check.rs:286` and `:608`) and the elaborator (`crates/elab/src/check.rs:1218`). Release builds have no overflow checks (no `overflow-checks` in Cargo.toml), so `Type u32::MAX : Type 0`. The parser accepts any level that fits in a u32 (`crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:3882`).

Consequence: the universe hierarchy is cyclic (Type 0 : ... : Type u32::MAX : Type 0), the setting of Girard's/Hurkens' paradox, so a proof of Void should be constructible (not built; treat as unsound). Also `Sort::fits_in` (term.rs:53-58) lets a Type 0 data type hold a field of type Type u32::MAX.

Fix direction: the kernel must refuse a universe whose successor doesn't exist (checked add, an error rather than saturating, since Type MAX : Type MAX is just as bad), the elaborator likewise, and the parser should keep levels far below the limit. Then audit the kernel for other unchecked arithmetic on levels, de Bruijn indices or counters. Must-reject tests for both programs above.

tickets.title: Consider congruence closure in cases (D2000): first show it would simplify existing proofs
tickets.body:
From the proof-automation research register (docs/research/proof-automation.md §5.1, ticket T1, decision D2000), redone from full texts 30 Oct 2026.

Idea: a congruence-closure step inside `cases`, as in Lean 4's `grind` and every SMT solver, using only the facts already in scope. Equations in scope are grouped into classes of equal terms, closed under "equal arguments give equal results". Two different constructors in one class makes the branch impossible; both sides of the goal in one class proves it. Stage 2 would apply each local ∀ hypothesis once to the matching facts. Probes that fail on main today (register §5.1): (1) `xs = Cons 1 Nil` and `xs = Nil` both in scope; (2) `f a = c` from `a = b` and `f b = c`; (3) `(y: Nat) → lookup = Some y → y < 5` with `lookup = Some y0`, goal `y0 < 5`.

Assumptions of D2000 in full: (A1) comparing class members by their computed form, as `cases` compares atoms now, is enough, without full conversion inside the closure; (A2) the classes at one `cases` node are small (tens of terms), so the step costs little when it fails; (A3) congruence steps written with `J`, with `Bool.uniqueEq` or `DecEq.uniqueEq` equating proof arguments, type-check for the dependent calls the target proofs contain.

D2000 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): NOT prioritised yet. First gather evidence that it would simplify EXISTING proofs. Before any design: survey std, examples, aoc and games/rogue proofs for steps that chain equations by hand (Eq.trans/Eq.sym/Eq.cong chains, rewrite sequences, matches that only exist to rule out a constructor clash, manual instantiation of a ∀ hypothesis) and that a congruence-closure step in `cases` would make unnecessary; count them, list file:line, and rewrite a few by hand-simulating the step to show the saving. Also cross-check against the cases follow-ups in SW-608. Prioritise only if the survey shows real savings.

tickets.title: Error enumeration for soundness testing (D2031): one type mismatch at every check site, kernel first
tickets.body:
D2031 (infrastructure register C3, §5.1 "Error enumeration", T2), from the Eris paper (Sotiropoulos and Su, PLDI 2026, doi 10.1145/3808320, read in full). Matt, 30 Oct 2026: backlog for now.

Idea: from an accepted program, at every place the checker compares an expression with a known expected type, substitute one expression of an incompatible type (one change per variant); every variant is ill-typed by construction, so any acceptance is a soundness lead. Stage K (kernel, small): over kernel terms, at the check sites in crates/core/src/check.rs (arguments, ascriptions, constructor fields, let values, case branches, definition bodies); oracle: refused with E-TYPE-MISMATCH / E-UNIVERSE / E-REFL; out-of-budget variants dropped. Stage E (elaborator, tooling): source-level, using the hover record of expected types; coercions, postponed comparisons and numeral defaults count as compatible. Options: (a) random overwrites in the existing 400-case daily fuzz run; (b) error enumeration, kernel first, on demand (task fuzz:enum) with a small daily sample. Recommendation: (b), stage K first. Assumptions in full: infrastructure.md §8, D2031.
